data.name: Ablaa
data.gender_notes: Ablaa is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who takes care of the grapes like a mother. The name Ablaa carries the meaning “Mother of Grapes” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Ablaa usually hope their child will grow to embody mother of grapes and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ablaa belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mother of Grapes.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ablaa total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_arabic.name: أبلا
in_arabic.meaning: ذات جمال و کمال، کامل، جمیل، منور، روشن، بصیرت
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم مؤنث مشتق از اب، به معنی بصیرت، فهم، ادراک، و درک حقایق. در فرهنگ اسلامی، ابلا به کسی که دارای فهم و بصیرت عمیق است اشاره دارد. این نام در میان زنان عرب و مسلمان به عنوان نمادی از خردمندی و درک عمیق استفاده می شود.

in_urdu.name: ابلا
in_urdu.meaning: جمیل، بصیرت، ادراک، دانشمند، دانا، خردمند
in_urdu.long_meaning: عربی میں اس نام کا مطلب ہے بصیرت، ادراک، اور فهم. اسلامی ثقافت میں، ابلا ایک ایسا نام ہے جو دانشمندی، دانائی، اور خردمندی کی علامت ہے. جنوبی ایشیائی مسلم معاشرے میں، یہ نام ان کی فطرت کی وجہ سے مقبول ہے.

in_hindi.name: अबला
in_hindi.long_meaning: हिन्दी में, अबला नाम का अर्थ है सुंदरता, ज्ञान, और बुद्धिमत्ता. इस्लामी परंपरा में, यह नाम बुद्धिमत्ता और उच्च समझ को दर्शाता है. भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम अपनी सुंदरता और अर्थ के कारण पसंद किया जाता है.

in_pashto.name: ابلا
in_pashto.long_meaning: په پښتو کې، ابلا د پوهې، پندارې، او ځانګړې کیدو معنی لري. په افغان او پښتني کلتور کې، دا نوم د پوهانې او حکمت نښه ده. دا نوم د ښکلا او سولې غوښتنې ته اشاره کوي.

in_english.name: Ablaa
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ablaa originates from Arabic roots, signifying beauty, insight, and understanding. In Islamic tradition, it denotes someone with deep perception and intelligence. Historically, the name reflects a blend of spiritual and aesthetic qualities, cherished across Muslim cultures for its profound meaning and elegant sound.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ablaa" holds significant cultural importance in Arabic communities due to its association with agriculture and the cultivation of grapes. In many Muslim cultures, grapes are considered a symbol of generosity, abundance, and blessings because of their lush growth in hot climates and the extensive process involved in their production. The name "Ablaa" can be likened to a nurturing mother who carefully tends to her vineyard, ensuring its continued growth and success.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, the care and cultivation of fruit trees, including grapes, hold deep spiritual significance. Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is recorded to have said, "The best of trees in earth are those which Allah caused to yield ghusl (a kind of ripe, fresh fig)." (Bukhari 4382) This hadith emphasizes the importance of seeking Allah's (Swt) blessings not only through spiritual practices but also through the cultivation of beneficial things, such as fruit trees, for the welfare of the community.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Ablaa means "Givers of Glad Tidings" in Arabic. It is a name given to those who bring joy, comfort, and hope to others, spreading positivity and happiness in their wake. It is a reminder of the importance of spreading love and kindness in our daily lives.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir, Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 11, Page 119 The name Ablaa carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ablaa bint Abi Sufyan was the wife of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and mother of his son Ibrahim. She was called Umm Ibrahim, and was originally named Ablah bint Abi Sufyan. Ablah converted to Islam during the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah in 6/624 CE. She later gave birth to Prophet Muhammad's son Ibrahim in 7/628 CE.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Baladhuri, Ansab Al-Ashraf, Volume 1, Page 120 The name Ablaa carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ablaa bint Abi Sufyan was a prominent woman of the Quraysh tribe who lived during the time of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). She was originally named Ablah but later changed her name to Ablaa due to a dream she had. In this dream, she saw herself serving water to the Prophet (pbuh) and his Companions during their Battle of Uhud in 3/625 CE. After the dream, she converted to Islam and became a devoted follower of the Prophet (pbuh). She later married the Prophet (pbuh) and gave birth to his son Ibrahim.
